title: Portaldot V3 pitfalls
subtitle: What breaks when you point ordinary EVM tooling at PortaldotV3 Test. Each entry says how to check it, what it costs you, and what to do instead. Measured 2026-10-18 → 2026-10-28 against wss://test-node-v3.portaldot.dev and https://test-evm-rpc-v3.portaldot.dev.

traps.title: An external EOA cannot send an EVM transaction at all
traps.symptom: eth_sendRawTransaction with every tx type, fee and gas combination returns {"code":1010,"message":"Invalid Transaction"}. Reads on the same endpoint answer normally.
traps.cost: A MetaMask/Remix workflow cannot complete its first write. Deploying from Remix fails too.
traps.workaround: Sign revive.call (or revive.instantiate_with_code) as a Substrate extrinsic with an sr25519 key: revive.call(dest, value, weight_limit, storage_deposit_limit, data). TwinKey is that path with a UI and an EIP-1193 provider.

traps.title: eth_estimateGas is off by four orders of magnitude
traps.symptom: A trivial call estimates in the 10^11–10^15 range while the block advertises gasLimit = u64::MAX, so any tool that auto-fills gas builds a transaction no balance can pay for.
traps.cost: Measured live on 2026-10-28: 570,540,468,341 vs 50,604,168 — 11,274×. A 401 tPOT wallet cannot cover a 50k-gas call priced at 5.7e11.
traps.workaround: Use ReviveApi_call's dry run: it returns weightRequired {refTime, proofSize} and storageDeposit.charge, which is exactly what revive.call consumes — and unused weight is refunded.

traps.title: eth_getLogs silently omits logs from native-origin calls
traps.symptom: eth_getLogs over the full block range for a contract that definitely emitted returns []. Our own contract emitted at blocks 90995, 102680, 102716, 227275 and appears zero times.
traps.check: POST eth_getLogs {fromBlock:0x0, toBlock:'latest', address:<your contract>} — compare with the events of the same block
traps.cost: Any indexer or dApp built on eth_getLogs is blind to every write that arrived through the native path — which, per the first entry, is every write.
traps.workaround: Read System.Events from the Substrate archive node and decode revive.ContractEmitted against your ABI. TwinKey's event feed and its /api/rpc receipts both do this.

traps.title: Native is 14 decimals, EVM is 18 — the ratio is 10,000
traps.symptom: The same balance reads 1.0000 on the Substrate side and 10000.000000000000000000 on the EVM side. nativeToEthRatio = 10000.
traps.cost: Every amount that crosses the boundary is wrong by 10,000×, in the direction that silently overpays.
traps.workaround: Keep bigint on both sides with an explicit decimal context; convert only at the boundary. TwinKey shows both denominators side by side rather than pretending there is one.

traps.title: The H160 is not derivable from the SS58 key
traps.symptom: Common derivations (first/last 20 bytes of the public key, keccak, blake2 truncation) produce an address the chain disagrees with; funds sent there are still visible but not spendable from the EVM side.
traps.check: curl state_call ReviveApi_address <accountId32-hex> → compare with any local derivation
traps.cost: Wrong msg.sender, wrong balance, and a wallet that looks funded but cannot act.
traps.workaround: Ask the runtime every time. TwinKey never derives locally, and says so in the UI.

traps.title: Only the EVM RPC prunes; the Substrate RPC is archival
traps.symptom: eth_call / eth_getBlockByNumber at a historical block fail with "UnknownBlock: State already discarded" beyond roughly 256 blocks, while state_getStorage at block 1 answers.
traps.check: eth_call at block N-1000 (fails) vs state_getStorage at the block hash (succeeds)
traps.cost: Historical verification looks impossible on the EVM side, so people conclude history is gone and start their index at today.
traps.workaround: Read history from the Substrate archive at a block hash; use the EVM endpoint only for current state and simulation. server-side: /verify reads archive, always.

traps.title: revive.instantiate_with_code wants constructor args inside the code blob
traps.symptom: Passing constructor calldata in the `data` field fails with revive.EvmConstructorNonEmptyData: "When calling an EVM constructor `data` has to be empty."
traps.check: any deployment with a constructor that takes arguments
traps.cost: An hour of confusion on the one path the official guide does not cover for parameterised constructors.
traps.workaround: code = creation_code + encodeAbiParameters(...); data = 0x; salt = null. tooling/deploy-token.mjs does exactly this.

traps.title: @polkadot/api needs RevealApi.instantiate's code as a ContractCode enum
traps.symptom: api.call.reviveApi.instantiate(origin, value, gas, deposit, <bytes>, data, salt) throws createType(...ContractCodeV1) Unable to create Enum via index 96.
traps.cost: The 7-argument runtime API is undocumented; the error points at SCALE, not at the argument.
traps.workaround: Pass { Upload: codeHex } instead of raw bytes.

traps.title: Both RPC hosts answer 403 without a User-Agent
traps.symptom: A bare fetch/reqwest from a server gets 403 with an empty body; curl works because it sends a UA.
traps.cost: Server-side integrations fail while the same code works in a browser, which reads as "the node is down".
traps.workaround: Set an explicit UA on every service client (the Rust verifier does).

traps.title: Native tPOT cannot be sent straight to an H160
traps.symptom: Air-dropping to 0x… leaves the native account empty and the EVM balance at zero.
traps.check: balances.transfer to the H160 vs to the H160's mapped SS58 via reviveApi.accountId
traps.cost: A funded-looking deployment that cannot pay for anything.
traps.workaround: Fund the native SS58 account; the mapping makes the balance visible on the EVM side (one-directional for funding).
